text:
maria: deploy-bot just flagged a canary latency regression in eu-west-1, p95 +180ms vs baseline at 20% traffic. thinking hold + quick triage. @ben @liz :eyes:

deploy-bot: Deployment id=2024.6.12-rc3 -> status=CANARY_HELD. reason=canary_p95_regression. threshold=150ms. auto-rollback eligible in 5m if metric persists.

ben: on it — pulling traces. any error-rate spike or just latency?

liz: logs show increased KV cache miss rate after the new kernel landed. sample from inference-proxy:
```
2024-06-12T14:07:10Z INFO request=abc123 kv_cache_hit=false backend=runtime-1 latency_ms=12
2024-06-12T14:07:10Z WARN request=abc124 kv_cache_hit=false backend=runtime-2 latency_ms=220
```
looks like prefix caching not warming fast enough.

maria: ok. i'd prefer manual rollback rather than letting auto-rollback flip the switch — want to coordinate customer comms first. can we set concrete rollback criteria?

samir: SRE POV: propose this as decision policy:
- if p95 > 150ms AND p50 > 40ms for 10m AND error-rate > 0.4% => auto rollback allowed
- if only p95 spike w/o errors => manual rollback after 5-10m triage

ben: +1. also: if KV-cache-miss rate > 10% sustained for 5m that's a hard signal.

maria: agreed. metrics currently: p95=182ms, p50=48ms, error-rate=0.12%, kv_miss=12% (5m window). meets kv_miss threshold but error-rate low. leaning manual rollback to preserve data and confirm root cause.

liz: can we try a quick mitigation: revert kernel flag "--fast-kv-path" on canary nodes to see if that recovers? if that fails, we rollback.

ben: im concerned toggling flags mid-rollout might diverge canary vs control. prefer rollback to last stable (v2024.6.11) for eu-west-1 canary slice.

maria: ok manual rollback. comms plan: 1) pin release notes and set status to "rollback in progress" on /releases 2) notify CS + small customer list 3) execute rollback 4) monitor for 10m then announce completion.

maria: running rollback now — command:```bash
redwoodctl rollout revert --region eu-west-1 --to v2024.6.11 --selector canary-slice --reason "canary p95 regression: kv_miss" --no-wait
```

deploy-bot: Rollback job accepted (job=rb-98321). ETA ~ 90s to cut traffic and redeploy.

oncall-bot: Note: outside normal change window (2:00-06:00 UTC) but emergency rollback authorized by oncall.

liz: drafting customer note for CS channel:
"We detected a latency regression in a limited canary rollout and reverted the new runtime kernel in eu-west-1 to ensure stable latency. No customer data was affected. We're investigating and will follow up with a root-cause and timeline for a safe re-release." :thumbsup:

ben: rollback finished, traffic pinned to v2024.6.11 for canary nodes in eu-west-1. pulling post-rollback metrics: p95=68ms (baseline 65ms), error-rate=0.07%, kv_miss=4%.

maria: nice. monitoring for 10m to be safe. thanks everyone. please add notes to the release ticket and mark release as "reverted - followup required".

samir: filing a short follow-up action item: investigate kv cache warmup regression + add a canary test that simulates cold-warm caches.

maria: closing this thread once the 10m window passes. will kick off postmortem doc and include suggested mitigations. :white_check_mark:
